features.title: Render inline references from other plugins
features.summary: Other plugins add a matcher and a React renderer to the inline-reference registry (@dshfiles/chat/inline-references); Chat applies them to assistant Markdown text runs, inline code and the Referenced-session line while it renders, so `b:12`, `@{luna}`, `memory: n:3` or `jj:main` become links without any plugin rewriting the transcript DOM. Higher priority wins an overlap, fenced code and links are never matched, and a streaming message's frozen blocks keep their rendered references.
failureModes: A matcher that throws is skipped for that run and logged once; the text stays as written.
A renderer that throws falls back to the matched text and is logged once.

verification.testName: lets the higher priority win an overlap, whatever the registration order
follows a streaming message: a reference completes as its text grows and frozen blocks keep their nodes

verification.reason: A registry with no UI of its own; the providers' journeys walk it in the browser (jujutsu.chat-references, agents.mention-preview, memory.reference-preview, mentions.session-mention-links).

telemetry.reason: Client-only: matching and rendering references in a message reads browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: Render fenced code blocks from other plugins
features.summary: Other plugins add a component for fence languages to the code-fence registry (@dshfiles/chat/code-fences); while Chat renders Markdown (assistant answers through InlineReferenceMarkdown; reasoning, compaction summaries and other plugins' Markdown through FencedMarkdown, @dshfiles/chat/fenced-markdown) it swaps each native code card whose language a renderer claims for that component, handing it the source, whether the fence may still grow (a fence followed by another block is complete even while the message streams), the native card as `fallback` and the highlighted code without its header as `source`. Fences nested in lists and quotes count, a streaming message's frozen blocks keep their rendered fences, and without renderers the native tree is unchanged.
failureModes: A renderer that throws shows the native code card and is logged once; new source for the same fence tries the renderer again.

keeps a frozen streaming block rendered once while the tail grows

shows the native card when a renderer throws, and tries again for new source

verification.reason: A registry with no UI of its own; the provider's journey walks it in the browser (mermaid-diagrams.chat-diagram).

telemetry.reason: Client-only: swapping a fence's element while a message renders reads browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: A finished turn folds its work under one Worked for row
features.summary: While a turn runs, its tail reads "Working for 12s" with a shimmer (paused off screen, none under reduced motion). Once it settles, its tool calls fold under one "Worked for 1m 12s" row; a failed call (an error result or a shell command that exited non-zero), a question and any PinnedToolCalls deliverable stay outside the fold, so a folded turn still shows what failed.
failureModes: A tool that reports failure only inside its own text (not isError, no [exit code: N] footer) folds like a success.

features.title: Choose Summary, Normal or Verbose for tool work
features.summary: Settings › General › View mode: Summary folds every turn’s tool work under one row, Normal folds finished turns, Verbose keeps every call open. Without a saved choice a touch phone gets Summary and other browsers Normal. The Agent reads it with transcript_view_get and sets or clears it with transcript_view_set (Chat’s own chat-view API on the same dshfiles-chat field), only when the user asked.

configuration.constraints: compact (Summary), detailed (Normal), verbose (Verbose); standard and legacy normal/expanded stay accepted. Without a saved value a coarse pointer gets compact; detailed is the default elsewhere.

failureModes: A read-only profile refuses transcript_view_set with SettingsReadOnly; the Settings row keeps the local choice for the session.

features.title: Find text anywhere in a long thread
features.summary: ⌘F in a thread (or Find in thread in its ⋯ menu, the phone's way in) opens a find bar: it asks session-search's index for every match in the whole thread, shows "n of N" counted from the newest, steps with ↵ (older) and ⇧↵ (newer), pages an unloaded Turn in, opens the Worked for fold, folded prompt or closed tool row that hides the match and highlights it. A second ⌘F while its field has focus is the browser's find. Without the index (not installed, thread not indexed yet) it searches the loaded Turns and says so; a failed search shows the reason and Retry.

features.title: Runs of background jobs and subagents fold into one summary row
features.summary: Two or more consecutive background-job or subagent rows fold into one row: "4 background jobs · 1 failed · 2 running · 1 done · longest 4m 10s", "3 subagents · 2 working · 1 finished", or one combined row when both kinds stand together. The row keeps live state (phase-synced spinner, the oldest running job's time on the shared second clock) and expands on click or Enter to the individual rows, each still expandable for output and its Stop/Open verbs; the choice holds while the page lives. A failed job or a subagent that needs you keeps its own row outside the fold, counted in red or indigo right after the total so a narrow row never truncates it. One row never folds; Verbose shows every row. Kinds come from the TranscriptRunFolds registry (`@dshfiles/chat/run-folds`), filled by background-jobs and thread-sidebar; without providers nothing folds.
features.currentSurface: transcript: summary row in place of the first row of the run
failureModes: A job that fails after its tool call settled stays outside the run fold, but the turn's own Worked for fold still hides it until opened: that fold is decided from the tool result, which reported success.
Runs are split by any other row between them (an assistant note, a different tool); same-turn rows that are not adjacent do not fold together.
